# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="push") — the large button
    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Pick the channel by the receiver, not by habit. A message sent in a sense they
  lack is not a message; it is a turn spent talking to the room.

- Exactly one of you can read the signs and still speak. Their spoken lines are
  the answer's only road to the hands, so spend them well.

- Agree on a small code before trading facts. A code invented mid-stream settles
  nothing, and one set first makes every later message cheap.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have no tactile information yet. Since the Mute can read the manual and can see my gestures, I will establish a compact gesture code for the Mute to pass to the Deaf next round. The Deaf should then inspect each visible feature and report verbally to the Mute, who can relay the results to me. I am asking the Mute now for the manual’s exact defusal procedure.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Please tell me the manual's exact defusal rules. I am defining a request code for Deaf: 👍 means display, 👎 means light, 👌 means button, ☝ means wire 1, ✌ means wire 2, 🤟 means wire 3. Please pass this code to Deaf next round and ask Deaf to report every requested value verbally to you.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👎", "👌", "☝", "✌", "🤟"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The bomb shows display 0, yellow light, and a large button marked PUSH TO DEFUSE. Wires are 1 red, 2 blue, 3 green. Mute is reading the manual and will relay the exact safe action.

The bomb’s perceptible facts are now complete: display 0, yellow light, button marked “PUSH TO DEFUSE,” and wires red, blue, green at positions 1–3. I still need the manual’s rule; I will ensure Mute has the full observation and ask for the single safe operation.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I received: display 0, yellow light, button PUSH TO DEFUSE, wire 1 red, wire 2 blue, wire 3 green. Please relay the manual's exact safe action now.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The bomb remains display 0, yellow light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires red blue green. I cannot interpret Mute's gestures; please follow Mute's spoken manual instruction exactly.

I still have the bomb’s physical details, but no manual instruction has reached me. Acting without the manual would risk detonating the bomb, so I will ask Mute to provide the exact operation rather than guess.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Your manual instruction did not reach me. State the exact safe action now, including whether to push or cut a wire and the wire position.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: No bomb change is visible: display 0, yellow light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires red blue green. Wait for Mute's spoken manual instruction; do not act on the gestures.

No manual instruction has arrived, so the safe action remains undetermined. I will not touch the bomb. I am reminding Mute that I need a spoken instruction directed to me; Deaf’s report cannot substitute for the manual.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I still have not received your manual instruction. Please speak directly to me now with exactly one literal action: push, or cut position 1, 2, or 3. I will act only on that instruction.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's latest message is two gestures, in order: thumbs down, then victory sign: ? ?. Bomb still shows display 0, yellow light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires red blue green.

Mute cannot speak, so the gestures are the only possible manual channel. I recognize the second gesture as ✌, which I previously assigned to wire 2, but the first gesture was not part of that wire code. I should not guess whether this means “do not push, cut wire 2” or something else. I will ask Deaf to relay the gestures exactly and ask Mute to use an unambiguous sequence based on the established code.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I received gestures thumbs down then victory through Deaf, but I cannot see gestures. Please resend using my agreed code: 👍 display, 👎 light, 👌 button, ☝ wire 1, ✌ wire 2, 🤟 wire 3. Use 👌 for push, or the wire symbol for cutting; do not add an unassigned gesture.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's newest message is one gesture: victory sign, ?. Previously Mute sent thumbs down followed by victory sign: ? ?. The bomb remains display 0, yellow light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires red blue green.

Mute’s latest unambiguous signal is ✌, which is my established code for wire 2. The earlier thumbs-down signal was not part of the agreed action code, but the repeated victory sign now identifies wire 2. I will cut the blue wire at position 2.

``` 
act(op="cut", position=2)
```
